newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kohl dismisses cabinet reshuffle rumours.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl dismisses cabinet reshuffle rumours.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl, facing record unemployment and deadlock over sweeping tax reforms, has dismissed rumours he planned a cabinet reshuffle, a German newspaper reported on Saturday.

According to a report in Welt am Sonntag released ahead of publication on Sunday, Kohl said he had no intention of giving up what he described an an "excellent" team. "With this team I will set about the tasks that lie ahead of us".
Stern weekly reported on Thursday that Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt was under pressure from the ranks of his Free Democrat Party (FDP) to resign citing a poor performance.
Rexrodt of the FDP, junior coalition partner to Kohl's Christian Democrats, laughed off the report.

The opposition Social Democrats (SPD) pulled out of talks to reach an agreement on major tax reforms with Kohl's ruling coalition in a recent clash over coal subsidy cuts, and has not yet agreed to return to the negotiating table.
Although Kohl's coalition holds a majority of seats in the Bundestag lower house of parliament, the SPD can block most tax measures through its majority in the Bundesrat upper house.
German unemployment stands at 4.7 million -- a post-war record high.
